requirements.reason: Permission addressed to producers about packaging. This implementation uses one representation; nothing follows for a verifier to check.

requirements.note: Reading: transport acknowledgements are not receiver-side records; they are accounted in the input accounting, outside |R|.

requirements.finding: Disposition when no issuer-side observation exists for an instruction in the population
readings: (a) INDETERMINATE (a reason other than ordinary absence of a receiver observation)
(b) INVALID (a required record is missing)
requirements.implemented: (a), and the instruction is reported as not dispatched
requirements.why: INVALID covers a required record that is malformed, fails verification or lacks a binding; an absent record is not named.

requirements.finding: Result of an emission that failed before the issuer boundary
readings: (a) EXPLICIT_FAILURE for each obligation of the attempt, scoped to the issuer boundary
(b) UNCONFIRMED with the failure kept as a diagnostic
(c) the instruction is excluded from I as never dispatched
requirements.implemented: (a); the instruction is reported as not dispatched
requirements.why: The failure is positive and attributable, but it is observed at the issuer boundary for all targets at once, while EXPLICIT_FAILURE is defined per attempt, target and boundary and must not be generalised to other targets.

requirements.note: Reading: an observer absent from the trust configuration gives INDETERMINATE (unresolved trust binding); an observer bound to another target gives an invalid receiver record and leaves the obligation as it was.

requirements.finding: NO_EFFECT is used in two dimensions and the control-effect vocabulary is not defined
readings: (a) NO_EFFECT in 5.7 is the enforcement value of 4.4
(b) NO_EFFECT in 5.7 is a control-effect result with its own vocabulary
requirements.implemented: (b): control-effect results EFFECT_OBSERVED, NO_EFFECT, UNKNOWN; NO_EFFECT requires predicate and window in both dimensions
requirements.why: 4.4 lists NO_EFFECT among enforcement outcomes, 5.7 forbids reporting silence 'as NO_EFFECT' in the control-effect section, and the appendix example uses UNKNOWN for control_effect without naming the other values.

requirements.finding: Deadline-elapsed negative observation: UNCONFIRMED or EXPLICIT_FAILURE
readings: (a) a deadline-elapsed record keeps the obligation UNCONFIRMED and is reported as a diagnostic
(b) a deadline-elapsed record is a positive, attributable failure observation and yields EXPLICIT_FAILURE
requirements.why: Case 10 says a missing acknowledgement WITHOUT a negative-observation record is UNCONFIRMED, not EXPLICIT_FAILURE, which reads as if the record would change the result; 5.8 says the record establishes only the reconciler's bounded view, and 9.1 lets a late receipt turn UNCONFIRMED into CONFIRMED.

requirements.note: Reduction rule: the profile's published precedence over the seven dispositions; every applicable disposition stays listed.

requirements.finding: Record class of a receiver record that addresses an expected obligation but does not confirm it
readings: (a) matched (it was correlated to the obligation, whose disposition is SUBSTITUTION, CONFLICT or INDETERMINATE)
(b) orphan (it matches no obligation in the CONFIRMED sense)
(c) a separate conflicting class
requirements.implemented: (a), with the matched class subdivided into confirming and non-confirming (6.4 allows subdivision that preserves the parent count)
requirements.why: 6.1 defines ORPHAN as matching no expected Delivery Obligation, while CONFIRMED is defined by a match of identifier, attempt, content, target and boundary; the word 'match' carries both meanings.

requirements.finding: Unresolved required target: INDETERMINATE by definition or INVALID by profile
readings: (a) always INDETERMINATE (6.1 names 'an unresolved required target' there)
(b) INDETERMINATE or INVALID as the profile declares (case 15)
requirements.implemented: (b): the profile declares the behaviour per case (unresolved, stale, ambiguous, inconsistent); vectors cover both choices
requirements.why: 6.1 places an unresolved required target under INDETERMINATE, while case 15 and 5.12 leave INDETERMINATE or INVALID to the profile.

requirements.reason: Addressed to a relying system's operational policy (fail-safe, retry, escalation). The report exposes the four states; choosing the local response is outside this verifier.

requirements.finding: Issuer-side identifier reuse with different content
readings: (a) SUBSTITUTION for every obligation of the instruction (9.1)
(b) CONFLICT (two issuer records make incompatible assertions)
(c) INVALID (the identifier rule of the profile is violated)
requirements.why: 6.1 defines SUBSTITUTION between issuer-side and receiver-side records; 9.1 says reusing one identifier for different content creates SUBSTITUTION without a receiver record being involved.

requirements.finding: Parent result of an instruction with zero obligations
readings: (a) not defined: neither fully confirmed nor not fully confirmed
(b) vacuously fully confirmed
(c) not fully confirmed
requirements.implemented: (a) (null), while a structural PASS may cover the instruction where the profile permits empty sets
requirements.why: 6.2 speaks only of 'a parent instruction that has one or more required targets'.

requirements.note: Duplicate selection rule: earliest observed time, then record id; the discarded record names the selected one.

readings: (a) one obligation per (instruction, required target); attempts are bindings inside it
(b) one obligation per (delivery attempt, required target), as the terminology also allows
requirements.why: Section 6.4 defines O = {(i,t) : i in I and t in T_i} over instructions. Under (b) |O| grows with retries and is no longer the set 6.4 counts, so a profile choosing (b) cannot use the 6.4 equation as written.

requirements.finding: Instruction-level equation has no class for a target resolution that fails or stays open
readings: (a) such an instruction counts in neither class; the draft equation does not balance and complete accounting cannot be claimed
(b) a third published class (not closed) is added beside the two, so every instruction stays accounted for
(c) the instruction is represented by placeholder obligations
requirements.implemented: (a) and (b) together: the report publishes the draft equation (fails) and an extended equation with the third class (balances); no complete-accounting claim
requirements.why: 5.11 requires every instruction to remain accounted for, 6.4 offers only with-obligations and zero-obligation classes, and 6.4 allows extra classes only for records, not for instructions. (c) conflicts with the spirit of 5.11-10 (no synthetic obligations).

requirements.finding: Which dispositions are positive failing conditions for FAIL
readings: (a) EXPLICIT_FAILURE and SUBSTITUTION
(b) EXPLICIT_FAILURE only
(c) also INVALID
requirements.why: 6.5 lists UNCONFIRMED, CONFLICT, INVALID and INDETERMINATE as preventing PASS but does not say which dispositions make FAIL; SUBSTITUTION rests on positive records that disagree, INVALID on a malformed record.

requirements.finding: Excluding an obligation 'before population construction' cannot depend on its disposition
readings: (a) the exclusion rule is decided on issuer-side attributes before any receiver evidence is used
(b) an obligation known to be UNCONFIRMED, CONFLICT, INVALID or INDETERMINATE may be excluded under a published rule
requirements.implemented: (a); the profile validator refuses exclusion rules over receiver-side attributes
requirements.why: Dispositions exist only after population construction (6.3), so (b) is circular and would allow the favourable-subset selection 10.3 warns about.

requirements.finding: Co-exposure when no relying-party claim is requested
readings: (a) the structural result always travels with an implicit claim ('the declared population reconciled under the profile's structural rules') and its support
(b) a structural result may only be exposed together with an explicitly requested claim
requirements.why: 6.6 requires 'the corresponding claim scope and claim-support qualification' wherever a structural result is exposed, but defines claim scope for claims exposed to a relying party; which claim corresponds when none is requested is not said.

requirements.reason: Addressed to protocol design (attachment points). Not a verifier behaviour.
Addressed to deployments (deadline definition). Not a verifier behaviour.
Addressed to deployments (binding paths into a Required Target Set). The per-obligation reconciliation it leads to is implemented under S5.10-1.

requirements.finding: 'Occurred before control activation' needs an ordering basis
readings: (a) without a supported ordering the crossing is neither protected nor blockable: indeterminate
(b) the reconciler orders by the asserted timestamps
requirements.why: 9.4 protects only crossings that actually occurred before activation; 5.9 says matching identifiers do not establish precedence and unsupported ordering claims must be omitted or indeterminate.

requirements.reason: Privacy practice for implementations in deployment. Not a verifier behaviour; the vectors carry no personal data.
Privacy default for producers. Not a verifier behaviour; vectors carry only small synthetic instruction content.
Privacy practice for profiles (commitments, nonces). Not implemented; digests here are unsalted and the vectors use synthetic content.

requirements.note: Every one of the 30 cases is exercised by at least one vector (tests/test_vectors.py checks this).
